figures.finding: For the 2026 charge year the first ZMW 61,200 of taxable income is tax-free, then 20% to 85,200, 30% to 110,400 and 37% above; the same rates apply to non-residents.

sources.said: The rates of income tax applicable to an individual for the 2026 charge year are as follows: Annual taxable income (ZMW) Rate of income tax (%) Up to 61,200 0 61,201 to 85,200 20 85,201 to 110,400 30 Over 110,400 37 In principle, the same rates apply to both Zambian and non-Zambian residents.

figures.finding: The charge year ends 31 December; a person with income outside PAYE files quarterly provisional returns and the final return and balance by 21 June of the next year.

sources.said: Income tax is determined by reference to a charge year, being the period of 12 months ending on 31 December.
The personal income tax return needs to be submitted by 21 June following the end of the tax year.

figures.finding: Employer and employee each pay 5% of gross earnings to NAPSA, capped at ZMW 1,861.80 a month each for 2026, and 1% of basic salary each to National Health Insurance.

figures.finding: Pay is taxed through PAYE; a small business with turnover between ZMW 12,000 and ZMW 5 million pays a 5% turnover tax instead of income tax and VAT (royalties excluded).

sources.said: A flat rate of 5% on business turnover will be applied where turnover is between ZMW 12,000 and ZMW 5 million per annum . Income that is subject to turnover tax will not be subject to income tax or VAT.

figures.finding: Public entertainment fees paid to a non-resident entertainer bear 20% withholding, a final tax for non-residents unless a treaty reduces it.

sources.said: Public entertainment fees to entertainers/sports persons N/A 20
Withholding tax is a final tax for nonresidents. The rates may be reduced under an applicable tax treaty.

figures.finding: Royalties bear 15% withholding when paid to a resident and 20% to a non-resident.
VAT is 16%; registration is required once turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZMW 800,000 a year.
